relationships.description: The sub-view region reads or writes records held in the persistent collection, for example listing or editing the rows of a table shown within its parent view.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view's data binding or the handler it invokes queries or mutates the named table, document collection or index, as shown by the repository call or query traced from that UI region.

relationships.description: The sub-view groups the component instance as one of its member parts, while the instance remains a separately identifiable placement that could be moved to another region.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view definition lists the component instance's id among its children or components array in the UX spec or layout file.

relationships.description: The sub-view draws the data it displays from the source and field path declared by the data-binding configuration.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view's spec entry carries a dataConfig or binding attribute that points to the configuration, or its code passes the configured store selector or API hook result into its children.

relationships.description: The sub-view is the screen region through which users carry out the steps of the business process, such as the approval panel in which an order-approval process is completed.
relationships.evidence: Design documentation or the sub-view's spec annotation maps the region's actions to the activities of the named business process, for example a trace link in the process model.

relationships.description: The sub-view is a concrete placement in a particular parent view of the reusable library sub-view definition it instantiates.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view's ref field names the library sub-view's id, or the parent view's markup embeds the shared library sub-view component.

relationships.description: The sub-view points to the object schema that describes the shape of the domain record it presents, without depending on it for runtime behavior.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view spec or its TypeScript props type references the schema's $id or the generated DTO or interface for the domain record.

relationships.description: When its parent view is displayed, the sub-view produces the visual output of the component instance at that instance's configured position with its prop values.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view's template or JSX emits the library component with the instance's props, matching the instance's render position in the UX spec.

relationships.description: The sub-view is shown or enabled only for users holding the permission, so the region is hidden or disabled for principals who lack that grant.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view is wrapped in a permission guard, or its spec declares a requiredPermission, or its visibility check calls the authorization helper with that permission's action and resource.

relationships.description: The sub-view provides the user-facing entry point through which consumers invoke the operations of the application service.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view's event handlers or submit actions call the application service's client or operations, for example a form region that triggers the service's create or update endpoint.

relationships.description: The sub-view applies the error display configuration to decide how failures in its region are surfaced, including whether a notification appears, its severity and its message text.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view spec references the error configuration id, or its error boundary or catch handler reads that configuration's severity and message text.

relationships.description: The sub-view arranges its child component instances according to the container rules of the layout configuration, such as grid tracks, spacing and alignment.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view's spec includes a layout reference to the configuration, or its container element carries the grid or flex classes and styles that the configuration defines.

relationships.description: The sub-view embeds the shared library sub-view composition and depends on it to supply the arrangement of components it shows.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view's ref attribute or an import in its source names the library sub-view, which is then mounted within the region.

notes: uses.ux.librarysubview duplicates realizes.ux.librarysubview, since both express the ref placement. Keep realizes. renders and aggregates of componentinstance overlap. Prefer composes for inline sub-views. uses.layoutconfig fits applies better. serves.applicationservice reverses the usual direction: the service serves the UI. accesses.collection skips the API layer.
